newsitem.title: GERMANY: German state investment in east fell in 1995.
newsitem.headline: German state investment in east fell in 1995.

text.p: Germany will maintain high public investment in the ex-communist east despite a fall in the value of government contracts there last year, Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Tuesday.
State contracts worth 16.5 billion marks were awarded in 1995 in the east, down by 6.5 billion marks, according to a report approved by Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet.
"It is right to keep this high level. We want in future to make a contribution to the economic regeneration of eastern Germany through public contracts," Rexrodt said in a statement.

Bonn has financed net annual transfers of over 100 billion marks to rebuild eastern Germany since unification in 1990, and the government last week promised to keep those transfers at a high level after current commitments run out in 1998.
